## 3.4 zsh-safe construction

The user runs zsh.

Do not rely on:

```text
unsetopt BANG_HIST
```

Instead make all patches safe by construction.

Avoid literal exclamation marks inside shell blocks, including heredocs.

When generated JavaScript/Rust requires an exclamation mark, the established safe technique is:

```python
bang = chr(33)
```

and use a placeholder such as:

```text
BANG
```

inside the heredoc, replacing it from Python before installing the file.

This pattern has been used successfully throughout the current work.

Compilation is allowed when it is genuinely useful.

Do not compile after every small patch.

# 5. CRITICAL Phase 8 / Following Doctrine

This is extremely important for the next session.

The original body of `FINAL_BETA.md` still contains older Phase 8 language that says:

```text
real signed follows
svc-index relationship storage
followers/following counts
network follow/unfollow routes
server relationship lookup
```

That old language is superseded by the later:

```text
FINAL_BETA_LOCAL_FOLLOWING_QUICKCHAIN_ADDENDUM_V1
```

The addendum explicitly supersedes conflicting requirements for:

```text
public follower counts
public following counts
public follower lists
public following lists
backend-custodied following lists
server-owned social graph edges
network follow/unfollow mutations
```

Current locked beta direction:

```text
FOLLOWING_LIST_OWNER=LOCAL_CRABLINK_APP
FOLLOWING_LIST_DEFAULT_STORAGE=LOCAL_DEVICE_STORAGE

PUBLIC_FOLLOWER_COUNT=FORBIDDEN
PUBLIC_FOLLOWING_COUNT=FORBIDDEN
PUBLIC_FOLLOWER_LIST=FORBIDDEN
PUBLIC_FOLLOWING_LIST=FORBIDDEN

NETWORK_FOLLOW_MUTATION=NOT_REQUIRED
SERVER_SOCIAL_GRAPH=NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_BETA
```

Core doctrine:

```text
Public content lives on the network.
Personal content selection lives on the user's device.
Verified delivery and eligible consumption evidence remain network-aware.
```

Correct local follow flow:

```text
user opens public creator profile
→ validates reviewed public profile reference
→ user presses Follow
→ CrabLink writes creator to reviewed local following record
→ profile displays local Following state
→ Home includes that creator during later public-timeline hydration
```

Correct unfollow:

```text
user presses Unfollow
→ local entry removed
→ later Home hydration excludes creator
→ existing cached items expire/remove under cache policy
```

Follow/unfollow must not:

```text
mutate svc-index relationship truth
create a public graph edge
change a follower counter
create an economic event
create a receipt
notify creator by default
claim network confirmation
require QuickChain
require ROX
require Solana
```

The public profile may display:

```text
identity
username
avatar
bio
public links
public publications
public media
public sites
pinned public content
local Follow / Following state
```

It must not display:

```text
public follower count
public following count
public follower list
public following list
social popularity rank based on follows
```

The addendum explicitly says the user's complete following list must not be uploaded merely to generate Home. 

The corresponding Home design is:

```text
HOME_FEED_COMPOSITION=LOCAL_FIRST
HOME_FEED_CONTENT_SOURCE=PUBLIC_NETWORK_TIMELINES
HOME_FEED_NETWORK_HYDRATION=REQUIRED_WHEN_ONLINE
HOME_FEED_OFFLINE_CACHE=OPTIONAL_AND_BOUNDED
HOME_FEED_ORDER=CHRONOLOGICAL
HOME_FEED_PUBLIC_SOCIAL_GRAPH_REQUIRED=NO
HOME_FEED_LOCAL_FOLLOW_LIST_REQUIRED=YES
```

Correct path:

```text
local following list
→ request each followed creator's public timeline
→ retrieve public publication records
→ verify metadata/content
→ merge timelines locally
→ deduplicate locally
→ chronological ordering
→ bounded verified local cache
→ render Home
```

This design is already supported by the Phase 6 creator-timeline work completed in this session. 

Therefore:

```text
DO_NOT_IMPLEMENT_OLD_SERVER_FOLLOW_GRAPH=YES
DO_NOT_ADD_PUBLIC_FOLLOW_COUNTS=YES
DO_NOT_UPLOAD_COMPLETE_FOLLOWING_LIST=YES
```

# 18. Phase 7A3 Apply Failure and Repair History

The first Phase 7A3 apply attempt failed before installing anything.

Failure:

```text
FINAL_BETA_PHASE7A3_PROFILE_TIMELINE_INTEGRATION=RED
FIRST_FAILURE=SCRIPTED_PHASE7A3_PATCH_FAILED
PATCH_RESULT=RED:PROFILE_PUBLIC_VIEW_FRAGMENT_MISSING:publicationClient.listCreatorPublications
PRODUCTION_SOURCE_CHANGED=NO
```

Cause:

The generated source formatted the call as:

```text
publicationClient
  .listCreatorPublications
```

while the patch's final guard searched for one contiguous literal:

```text
publicationClient.listCreatorPublications
```

This was not a code defect.

It was a whitespace-sensitive validation defect.

V2 changed validation to a whitespace-normalized semantic check.

V2 applied successfully:

```text
FINAL_BETA_PHASE7A3_PROFILE_TIMELINE_INTEGRATION_V2=APPLIED
FIRST_FAILURE_FIXED=WHITESPACE_SENSITIVE_PUBLICATION_CLIENT_GUARD
PATCH_VALIDATION=WHITESPACE_NORMALIZED_SEMANTIC_SOURCE
```

Production integration then installed cleanly.

This is another reminder for future source guards:

```text
Prefer semantic/whitespace-normalized matching where formatting is expected
to wrap function calls or JSX props.
```

Do not use brittle contiguous-string guards for rustfmt/prettier-style source.

```text
packages/crablink-core
  LocalFollowingRecordV1 normalization/validation if appropriate

  profile Follow / Following / Unfollow UI

Home later:

  locally merges them
```

```text
{
```

```text
device private key

wallet authority
private profile information
invented usernames
invented ownership claims
```

# 22. Phase 9 — Correct Home Feed Interpretation

The original generic buildplan says "following feed backend," but the superseding design means the beta should not upload the complete local follow list to a server feed endpoint.

Correct architecture:

```text
local following record
→ for each followed creator:
     Phase 6 public creator timeline reads
→ validate PublicationPageV1
→ merge locally
→ deduplicate
→ chronological order
→ bounded cache
→ Home rendering
```

Network provides public truth.

Client provides private selection.

Home feed should be:

```text
chronological
transparent
no engagement ranking
no paid ranking
no surveillance-based ranking
```

Offline cache may render prior verified summaries with stale/offline labels.

It may not invent:

```text
new follows
new posts
deletion truth
paid entitlement
freshness
```

# 41. Authority Boundaries to Preserve

```text
React:
  display
  local feed composition
  explicit user intent

Tauri:
  native privilege
  reviewed local persistence
  secure Passport surfaces
  bounded native operations

svc-passport:
  Passport identity
  device authorization
  capability truth

svc-index:
  public lookup
  public creator timeline projections
  public content indexes
  no economic truth
  no required beta follower graph

svc-wallet:
  approved economic mutation ingress

ron-ledger:
  durable balances
  receipts
  economic truth

ron-accounting:
  deterministic accounting snapshots
  not balance truth

svc-rewarder:
  bounded reward planning
  no direct ledger mutation

QuickChain:
  deterministic evidence commitment
  replay
  confirmation
  challenge
  not client authority

ROX Anchor:
  controlled private-testnet external anchor
  not the internal ROC ledger
```

# 47. Verification Philosophy Learned From This Session

Several failures were caused by brittle source assertions rather than production behavior.

Future source tests/patch guards should prefer:

```text
semantic markers
regex across whitespace
split_whitespace normalization
whitespace-stripped compact source
behavioral focused tests
```

Avoid assuming formatting like:

```text
foo.bar()
```

when actual source may format as:

```text
foo
  .bar()
```

Similarly, do not forbid generic words that are present in explanatory comments.

Prefer code-shaped forbidden guards such as:

```text
/v1/index/
svcIndex
svc_index
omnigate.request
```

over generic prose tokens.

# 3. Important Superseding Social Product Doctrine

The old generic FINAL_BETA language around a server-hosted Follow Graph was superseded by the later local-following product decision.

Do not accidentally regress to the old architecture.

The locked current model is:

```text
FOLLOWING_LIST_OWNER=LOCAL_CRABLINK_APP
FOLLOWING_LIST_DEFAULT_STORAGE=LOCAL_DEVICE_STORAGE

PUBLIC_FOLLOWER_COUNT=FORBIDDEN
PUBLIC_FOLLOWING_COUNT=FORBIDDEN
PUBLIC_FOLLOWER_LIST=FORBIDDEN
PUBLIC_FOLLOWING_LIST=FORBIDDEN

NETWORK_FOLLOW_MUTATION=NOT_REQUIRED
SERVER_SOCIAL_GRAPH=NOT_REQUIRED_FOR_BETA
COMPLETE_FOLLOWING_LIST_UPLOAD=FORBIDDEN
```

Product doctrine:

```text
public content lives on the network
personal selection lives on the user's device
```

Follow and unfollow are local user-selection operations.

They are not:

```text
wallet operations
ledger operations
QuickChain operations
receipts
network relationship mutations
economic events
```

Creators may still receive QuickChain/ROC rewards through the independent content/economic system.

The client does not need a global follower graph to create the Home experience.

---

# 4. Home Feed Architecture That Must Remain Locked

The Home feed architecture is:

```text
local following record
→ read each followed creator's public timeline
→ validate canonical publication pages
→ merge locally
→ deduplicate locally
→ deterministic chronological ordering
→ bounded display
→ bounded verified local cache
```

The network provides:

```text
public creator/content truth
```

The client provides:

```text
private selection of creators to follow
```

Home ordering remains:

```text
chronological
```

Explicitly forbidden:

```text
opaque engagement ranking
paid ranking
surveillance-based ranking
global feed cursor authority
complete following-list upload
public follower counters
public following counters
```

## 6.3 What A6 proves

The local Home cache remains:

```text
schema:
  crablink.local-following-feed-cache.v1

maximum items:
  50

content:
  validated public publication summaries only

ordering:
  deterministic chronology
```

Current local follows gate cached visibility.

Therefore:

```text
CURRENT_LOCAL_FOLLOWS_GATE_VISIBILITY=YES
UNFOLLOW_HIDES_CACHED_CREATOR=YES
ABSENT_FOLLOWING_TRUTH_SHOWS_CACHE=NO
```

An old cached creator does not remain visible after that creator is no longer locally followed.

The cache does not rewrite itself merely because the user unfollows someone.

The projection simply stops exposing that creator.

## 6.4 Offline truth posture

Offline cache status is always:

```text
stale-offline
```

It does not claim:

```text
freshness
deletion truth
relationship truth
ranking truth
network confirmation
```

The Home UI visibly labels stale cached content as previously verified local display.

Existing user-facing stale copy was proven present.

The cache may help display prior verified public summaries.

It may not become a truth oracle.

## 6.5 Paid-content boundary

A cached publication may preserve:

```text
access: paid
```

but that is only display metadata.

The cache cannot create:

```text
paid entitlement
paid unlock
receipt authority
wallet authority
ledger authority
network confirmation
```

The paid asset and paid site access components were checked and remain dependent on live backend payment/confirmation behavior.

Therefore:


## 6.6 Cache persistence boundary

Desktop cache persistence remains behind fixed native commands:

```text
local_following_feed_cache_read
local_following_feed_cache_write
```

No new browser-storage bypass was introduced.

No direct network fetch path was added to the cache adapter.

# 22. Phase 11A1 Developer Boundary

`SiteGuidedSetup.jsx` now derives:

```text
customCodeEnabled
```

from the shared explicit developer surface contract.

The effective requirement is:

```text
import.meta.env.DEV === true
AND
app.settings.devMode === true
```

Therefore:

```text
release build + devMode false:
  hidden

release build + stale devMode true:
  hidden

development build + devMode false:
  hidden

development build + devMode true:
  retained internal custom-code controls may appear
```

This preserves a useful internal testing surface without exposing it to normal beta users.

# 27. Phase 11A2 New Policy Module

New file:

```text
apps/crablink-tauri/src/pages/site/siteCustomHtmlPolicy.js
```

Policy schema/version:

```text
crablink.site-custom-html-policy.v1
```

Primary functions:

```text
reviewSiteCustomHtml(value)
acceptSiteCustomHtml(value)
```

The policy is:

```text
deterministic
local
pure
fail-closed for the targeted forbidden classes
```

It does not make backend/network calls.

It does not mutate wallet, ledger, QuickChain, or ROX state.

---

# 28. Phase 11A2 Forbidden Custom HTML Classes

The policy now rejects the following required classes.

## JavaScript elements

Example:

```html
<script>...</script>
```

Finding:

```text
custom_javascript
```

## JavaScript URLs

Examples in:

```text
href
src
action
formaction
```

such as:

```text
javascript:...
```

Finding:

```text
custom_javascript
```

## Arbitrary forms

The policy rejects:

```html
<form>
```

and standalone form controls including:

```html
<input>
<select>
<textarea>
```

Finding:

```text
arbitrary_form
```

## Iframes

Rejected:

```html
<iframe>
```

Finding:

```text
iframe
```

## Inline event handlers

Rejected patterns include attributes such as:

```text
onclick=
onload=
onerror=
...
```

Finding:

```text
event_handler
```

## Remote HTTP/HTTPS resources

The policy checks remote references in:

```text
src
href
poster
action
formaction
```

including protocol-relative URLs.

Finding:

```text
remote_resource
```

## Remote srcset resources

Remote URLs in:

```text
srcset
```

are rejected.

## Remote CSS imports/resources

The policy rejects remote resource usage through:

```css
@import ...
url(...)
```

when those target HTTP(S) or protocol-relative external resources.

Finding:

```text
remote_resource
```

# 34. Important Security Interpretation of A2

Do not overclaim what A2 is.

A2 is a deterministic rejection boundary for the explicit beta-forbidden classes.

It is not a complete general-purpose HTML security proof.

Do not claim:

```text
all possible hostile markup is impossible
all HTML parser edge cases are solved
all CSS attacks are solved
all SVG attacks are solved
all browser sandbox escapes are solved
```

Phase 11 still requires:

```text
safe theme token allowlist
declarative embed allowlist
sandbox defense in depth
formal malicious-input / release-mode closeout
```

Phase 22 later performs broader:

```text
sandbox malicious corpus
parser fuzzing
origin review
capability review
secret review
privilege separation
```

Therefore A2 should be viewed as:

```text
required beta input rejection boundary
+
one layer of defense in depth
```

not:

```text
the only site security mechanism
```

# 42. Failed-Patch Lessons to Carry Forward

## Lesson 1 — Verify actual component ownership first

Do not assume:

```text
SiteLaunchFlow
```

owns controls merely because it is the page-level flow.

The real control owner was:

```text
SiteGuidedSetup
```

Inspect live ownership first.

## Lesson 2 — Avoid brittle full-copy anchors

Do not anchor mutation correctness to large exact prose strings unless absolutely necessary.

Prefer:

```text
function names
component tags
unique field labels
stable imports
stable DTO/schema names
```

## Lesson 3 — Python inside shell must be Python

Do not use shell idioms such as standalone:

```text
:
```

inside Python heredocs.

Use:

```python
pass
```

## Lesson 4 — Test behavior, not invented terminal markers

Do not assert that test source contains terminal output labels unless the source intentionally defines those labels.

Prefer actual behavior/assertions.

## Lesson 5 — Respect actual function contracts

Do not infer signatures from names.

Example:

```text
primaryNavigationIdForRoute
```

expects a parsed route shape, not necessarily a route string.

Inspect implementation or existing regressions.

---

# 43. Shell / Terminal Rules That Remain Mandatory

All future terminal patches must remain compatible with the established workflow.

## No Git commands

Do not include:

```text
git status
git diff
git add
git commit
git push
git apply
```

or any other Git commands.

The user handles repository operations separately.

## Two-step mutation / verification flow

Preferred:

```text
Turn 1:
  APPLY-ONLY

user pastes output

Turn 2:
  VERIFICATION-ONLY
```

Do not bake large verification suites into mutation patches.

## zsh safety

Avoid shell content that can trigger zsh history expansion.

Especially avoid literal unsafe unquoted:

```text
!
```

Do not solve this by changing shell history settings.

Write inherently safe shell blocks.

## Functions

Prefer:

```bash
some_patch_function() {
  ...
  return 0
}
```

Do not use:

```bash
exit
```

inside patches intended for interactive terminal paste.

## Fix first failure

When RED:

```text
identify the first real failure
patch only that failure
rerun the focused check
```

Do not expand scope while the first failure remains.

The formal Phase 15 goal includes categories, thread lists, thread creation, reply chains, sticky/locked state, moderation labels, pagination, latest activity, and reviewed creator/moderator controls, with Forum and Imageboard required to reuse the same Post/Comment/thread/reply contracts.

# 3. Mandatory development workflow to preserve

The next session should continue the established mutation discipline.

```text
PATCH_WORKFLOW:
  1. inspect when necessary
  2. apply-only mutation block
  3. inspect user terminal output
  4. verification-only block
  5. fix first failure before expanding scope

DO_NOT:
  combine mutation and verification
  include git commands
  regenerate codebundle after every patch
  run full release builds after trivial changes
  use Node --check on JSX
  use top-level set -euo pipefail
  rely on zsh history-expansion workarounds
  include unsafe unquoted exclamation syntax

VERIFICATION_POLICY:
  JS/model/source changes:
    focused Node tests / source tests

  JSX:
    Vite transform/parser validation where needed

  Rust:
    focused cargo test/check for changed crate

  full frontend/Tauri/release build:
    phase closeout
    major integration boundary
    release gate
    or when failures genuinely require it

MANUAL_ACCEPTANCE:
  use concise chat checklist
  user reports GREEN / RED / SKIPPED
  do not force an interactive questionnaire script
```

No `git status`, `git diff`, `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`, or other Git commands should be included in assistant-generated terminal patches.

# 4. Locked product and authority boundaries

These rules remain fundamental and were actively protected during this session.

```text
CRABLINK:
  display + user intent

TAURI:
  native privileged client boundary

RUSTYONIONS:
  durable backend/network truth

svc-passport:
  identity / Passport claim truth

svc-index:
  lookup/discovery/projection metadata
  NOT wallet or identity ownership authority

svc-wallet:
  approved economic ingress

ron-ledger:
  internal ROC economic truth

QUICKCHAIN:
  network/finality rules remain backend-owned
  CrabLink display-only for finality

ROX_ANCHOR:
  private Solana-testnet anchor path
  NOT internal ROC ledger
```

The FINAL_BETA architecture explicitly keeps durable truth in RustyOnions services and prevents client/display state from becoming economic or consensus authority. Arbitrary decentralized code execution, public ROX bridging, production mint/burn, staking, liquidity, and exchange-facing behavior remain outside the desktop beta.

# 10. Phase 15A4 started as a public-read/category problem

The original A4 objective was straightforward:

```text
Forum thread list must be built from durable public backend data.

Forum category must come from durable public truth.

Forum replies must come from the existing durable Comment relation system.

Forum sticky/locked truth must come from reviewed policy.

Latest activity must be backend-derived.

Pagination must remain bounded.
```

The first architectural inspection found a real gap.

CrabLink A3A already wrote:

```text
forum

forum-category:<category>
```

into the canonical Post tags.

Omnigate already transported Post tags into the immutable manifest.

However, the existing canonical `PublicationSummaryV1` public creator projection did **not** expose tags.

This meant:

```text
Forum creation:
  knew category

immutable Post manifest:
  knew category

public creator PublicationSummaryV1:
  LOST category
```

Defaulting all publicly-read threads to `general` would have been incorrect.

Using `sessionStorage` or the local creation intent as public truth would also have been incorrect.

This drove the deeper A4 inspection rather than implementing a fake local workaround.

but there was no real production writer feeding the creator-publication projection.

Most existing appearances of `PublicationSummaryV1` construction were fixtures/tests.

This was broader than Forum.

The public timeline/feed/Explore/read models could exist structurally while their durable production projection remained unpopulated.

That led to A4A1.

# 15. Critical security correction made during A4

At this point the plan was initially:

```text
Post publish
→ resolve owner Passport subject in svc-passport
→ construct verified PublicationSummaryV1
→ write creator-publication projection
```

That plan was deliberately **stopped** after deeper inspection.

Reason:

```text
request.owner_passport_subject
```

is not itself proof that the caller controls that Passport.

Likewise:

```text
x-ron-passport
```

is context, not sufficient user ownership proof.

The existing `svc-passport /verify` surface was also inspected.

It verifies an Ed25519 envelope but does not give a trustworthy binding equivalent to:

```text
the current desktop publisher cryptographically proved control
of this local Passport subject for this publication
```

The current native desktop bridge does not expose an appropriate user-Passport authorship-signature/capability primitive for this exact purpose.

Therefore:

```text
DO_NOT:
  use owner_passport_subject as verified authorship

DO_NOT:
  use x-ron-passport as verified authorship

DO_NOT:
  parse username from Passport subject

DO_NOT:
  use creatorDisplay as canonical username

DO_NOT:
  pretend /verify proves publisher ownership when it does not
```

This was an important architectural correction.

Consequences:

```text
creator-publication PUT:
  remains implemented
  remains GREEN
  remains intentionally unwired

svc-passport by-subject lookup:
  remains implemented
  remains GREEN
  but does not alone prove current publisher control

Forum public read:
  shifted to Site-root projection with display-only creator text
```

This must be preserved in the next session.

# 16. Existing Comment relation architecture inspected

The existing durable relation subsystem was examined as a possible Forum root source.

It is intentionally:

```text
schema:
  crablink.publication-relation.v1

publication kind:
  Comment only

keying:
  exact parent crab URL

supports:
  parent
  optional thread root
  exact Site
  creatorDisplay
  created_at_ms
  visibility
  manifest/content/Site references
```

Validation explicitly rejects non-Comment relation sources.

The store uses:

```text
publication_relation:<parent>:<publication-id>
```

The HTTP surface:

```text
PUT /v1/index/publication-relations

GET /v1/index/publication-relations?parentCrabUrl=<typed asset>
```

This model is correct for replies, but wrong for Site-level thread discovery.

Widening it to include Post roots would have blurred:

```text
Site root discovery

vs.

parent/reply topology
```

Therefore it was left unchanged.

The uploaded inspection confirms the relation model is Comment-only and exact-parent keyed, while no prior Site-publication keyspace existed.

```text
CARGO_CHECK_RUN=NO

NEXT_ACTION=
RUN_PHASE15A4A2B2_FOCUSED_OMNIGATE_POST_TESTS_AND_CHECK
```

### What A4A2B2 changed

`TextAssetPublishResponse` now has an optional:

```text
site_publication_index
```

status object for Post publication.

A Site-publication write is attempted for:

```text
TextAssetKind::Post
```

only.

Not currently:

```text
Article
Image
Comment
```

Comment continues to use:

```text
publication_relation
```

### Ordering enforced by the new logic

The intended sequence is:

```text
paid content upload succeeds
→ canonical asset CID exists
→ manifest write exists
→ existing asset→manifest index pointer stores successfully
→ canonical Post crab URL exists
→ Site-publication root write is attempted
```

The Site-publication write is skipped if the existing asset index pointer did not reach:

```text
stored
```

This deliberately prevents public Site discovery from outrunning the core asset/manifest index.

### Timestamp source

The patch changed timestamp extraction into a reusable:

```text
publication_created_at_ms
```

read from the already-created immutable content envelope.

Comment relation ordering continues to use that value.

Post Site-root ordering also uses it.

This avoids creating a new index-write-time timestamp.

### Site-root Post write body

The Omnigate helper constructs:

```text
schema:
  crablink.site-publication.v1

publicationId:
  raw B3 hash

kind:
  post

crabUrl:
  canonical .post URL

title:
  canonical Post title projection

summary:
  bounded relation_summary_text(body)

creatorDisplay:
  display-only request value

createdAtMs:
  immutable content envelope timestamp

visibility:
  request visibility

references:
  manifestCid
  contentCid
  siteUrl

tags:
  normalized original Post tags

siteCrabUrl:
  exact Site
```

This is exactly how Forum category information reaches durable public discovery:

```text
Forum draft:
  forum
  forum-category:<category>

→ Post request

→ immutable manifest

→ Site-publication projection

→ future Forum public reader
```

### Failure behavior

A failure writing the Site projection does **not** pretend that indexing succeeded.

It reports:

```text
stored
failed
or skipped
```

plus truthful warnings.

It also does not retroactively claim that successfully stored immutable Post bytes never existed.

This is the correct distinction between:

```text
content publication success

and

secondary discovery projection success
```

### Existing integration test extension

`crates/omnigate/tests/text_asset_publish.rs` was extended so the dummy index accepts:

```text
PUT /v1/index/site-publications
```

and checks the Site-publication payload.

The test Post now carries:

```text
post
backend
forum
forum-category:general
```

The existing successful Post publish test was extended to require:

```text
site_publication_index.status = stored

site_publication_index.route =
  /v1/index/site-publications

site_publication_index.http_status = 202
```

**None of this has been compiled/tested yet.**

# 22. Important data-model split now established

The next session must understand the distinction between the three public metadata systems.

## Creator-publication projection

```text
PublicationSummaryV1

key:
  creator username + publication ID

purpose:
  creator timeline
  Home/Explore/profile-style publication discovery

identity shape:
  canonical creator username/profile

current writer:
  generic svc-index PUT exists

production Omnigate wiring:
  intentionally NO
```

Reason it is unwired:

```text
current publish request lacks sufficient proof
that caller controls claimed Passport subject
```

## Site-publication root projection

```text
crablink.site-publication.v1

key:
  named Site + publication ID

purpose:
  Site-level root discovery
  Forum Post roots
  later potentially Image/Article roots

identity shape:
  creatorDisplay only

current writer:
  Omnigate Post path applied
  awaiting verification
```

## Publication relation projection

```text
crablink.publication-relation.v1

key:
  exact parent + relation publication ID

purpose:
  Comment/reply topology

root kind:
  Comment only

current writer:
  existing Omnigate Comment path

status:
  established and preserved
```

This separation is intentional.

Do not collapse these models together.

# 23. Forum tag contract

The Forum category contract is now:

```text
generic Forum marker:
  forum

category marker:
  forum-category:<normalized-category>
```

A Forum-created Post gets these tags through `forumProductFlow.js`.

`PostPublishFlow.jsx` passes tags into the real Post publish payload.

Omnigate already normalizes/preserves them in the Post publication/manifest path.

The new Site-publication root projection also carries those normalized tags.

This solves the original A4 category-truth problem without adding a Forum-specific database field.

# 24. Creator identity posture to preserve

This is one of the most important session outcomes.

```text
creatorDisplay:
  convenience/display text

creatorDisplay:
  NOT identity authority

owner_passport_subject:
  publication ownership/reference context

owner_passport_subject:
  NOT proof of caller control by itself

x-ron-passport:
  context

x-ron-passport:
  NOT sufficient authorship proof

svc-passport by-subject lookup:
  confirms a stored claim exists

svc-passport by-subject lookup:
  DOES NOT by itself prove current caller controls subject

verified creator username in Site root:
  NO

profile URL in Site root:
  NO
```

A future creator-publication writer should only be wired when the system has a real caller-to-Passport authorship proof that cannot be forged by simply naming another subject.

Do not weaken this in order to make timelines populate faster.

# 4. Important checkpoint protocol decision made this session

A critical checkpoint-versioning issue was discovered and resolved.

The pre-existing:

```text
QuickChainUnsignedCheckpointPayloadV1
```

is a frozen Phase-0/local-root artifact.

It deliberately rejects committee/finality-era commitments such as:

```text
validator_set_hash
data_availability_root
```

It would have been incorrect to mutate that locked V1 payload because doing so could break existing golden vectors and hash contracts.

Instead, an additive payload was created:

```text
QuickChainCommitteeCheckpointPayloadV1
schema = quickchain.committee-checkpoint-payload.v1
```

The old payload remains unchanged.

This new payload requires:

```text
validator_set_hash
data_availability_root
```

but still explicitly contains **no validator signatures**.

It reuses the existing checkpoint hash domain:

```text
quickchain.checkpoint.v1
```

No new domain separator was introduced.

This is deliberate.

Future code should not casually merge or replace these two contracts.

---

# 5. Receipt-root provenance work completed before checkpoint assembly

Another important checkpoint safety issue was discovered earlier in the session.

The checkpoint header names its receipt-root scheme as:

```text
LedgerSequenceMerkleV1
```

but the general-purpose tree reducer accepts generic sort keys.

Simply accepting any generic `Receipts` root and labeling it `LedgerSequenceMerkleV1` would have overclaimed provenance.

The protocol's canonical receipt ordering was confirmed to be:

```text
u64_be(ledger_seq_start) || utf8(txid)
```

and `ron-proto` already owned the canonical helper for that ordering.

Therefore `ron-ledger` received a typed receipt-root producer instead of trusting arbitrary generic receipt roots.

Relevant implementation:

```text
crates/ron-ledger/src/quickchain/tree_material_projection.rs
```

Added typed wrapper:

```text
QuickChainLedgerSequenceReceiptRoot
```

and producer:

```text
compute_ledger_sequence_receipt_root(...)
```

Properties:

* validates each immutable receipt hash payload;
* rejects cross-chain receipt material;
* obtains exact sort-key semantics from `ron-proto`;
* hashes receipt payloads under:
  `quickchain.receipt.v1`;
* feeds the existing audited sorted Merkle reducer;
* does not expose an arbitrary constructor from a generic root;
* does not perform checkpoint assembly;
* does not perform validator signing;
* does not perform finality.

Focused suite:

```text
cargo test -p ron-ledger \
  --features quickchain-preflight \
  --test final_beta_phase19_receipt_root_semantics
```

Final result:

```text
running 9 tests
...
test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed
```

The tests prove:

1. empty typed receipt root matches existing empty receipts root;
2. input permutation does not change root;
3. root matches ledger-sequence-then-txid protocol material;
4. equal sequence uses txid tie-break deterministically;
5. cross-chain receipts reject;
6. invalid receipt payload rejects;
7. duplicate `(ledger_seq_start, txid)` sort key rejects;
8. immutable payload change changes root;
9. typed wrapper preserves receipt provenance.

Therefore:

```text
PHASE19_LEDGER_SEQUENCE_RECEIPT_ROOT=GREEN
RECEIPT_ORDERING_PROVEN=GREEN
RECEIPT_ROOT_PROVENANCE=GREEN
GENERIC_RECEIPT_ROOT_AS_CHECKPOINT_TRUTH=NO
```

# 6. Static scanner failure and repair

After the typed receipt-root work, the behavioral suite was GREEN but:

```text
quickchain_pre_root_boundary
```

failed.

The scanner reported:

```text
found forbidden token `ring::`
```

in:

```text
src/quickchain/tree_material_projection.rs
```

This was a **false positive**.

Cause:

```rust
String::with_capacity(...)
```

lowercased to:

```text
string::with_capacity
```

and the scanner naïvely searched for the substring:

```text
ring::
```

which appears inside `string::`.

We did **not** weaken the scanner and did **not** add a broad exception.

Instead the local buffer creation was rewritten scanner-safely using a default `String` plus `reserve`.

Apply:

```text
FINAL_BETA_PHASE19_RECEIPT_ROOT_RING_FALSE_POSITIVE_REPAIR=APPLIED
FAILURE_CLASS=STATIC_SCANNER_SUBSTRING_FALSE_POSITIVE
SCANNER_POLICY_CHANGED=NO
SCANNER_EXCEPTION_ADDED=NO
RECEIPT_ROOT_ALGORITHM_CHANGED=NO
```

Boundary rerun:

```text
running 2 tests
test phase5_anchor_checkpoint_exception_is_narrow ... ok
test quickchain_preflight_sources_have_no_runtime_authority_or_root_production ... ok

test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed
```

Then the 9 receipt-root tests were rerun and remained GREEN.

Important lesson for later patches:

> The source-boundary scanners perform substring-based checks after stripping comments/literals. Innocent namespace syntax can trip them. Prefer fixing the local spelling/structure rather than widening scanner exceptions unless the new authority surface is genuinely intentional.

# 8. Canonical transition identity foundation

Before live signing was possible, the session fixed a serious protocol-authority seam.

Previously the reward-loop integration test constructed its transition hash from a **test-local identity struct**.

That meant production macronode signing risked either:

* trusting a caller-supplied transition hash; or
* duplicating the test-local preimage contract.

Neither was acceptable.

The canonical transition identity was therefore moved into `ron-proto`.

```text
RocEpochTransitionIdentityV1
```

# 10. Exact transition-hash contract

The transition identity hash contract currently used by the reward/quorum path is:

```text
BLAKE3(
    domain_bytes
    || 0x00
    || serde_json::to_vec(identity)
)
```

with:

```text
domain = phase22.epoch-transition.v1
```

wrapped as:

```text
b3:<64 lowercase hex>
```

The macronode signing path recomputes this locally.

The caller does **not** supply the transition hash.

This is an important invariant.

# 12. Signature reuse test failure and repair

An early signer test failed:

```text
signature_cannot_be_reused_for_a_different_valid_identity
```

The production behavior was correct.

The test incorrectly expected:

```rust
kms.verify(...).is_err()
```

for a validly encoded but cryptographically mismatching Ed25519 signature.

The verifier actually returns:

```text
Ok(false)
```

for that case.

The test was repaired to:

1. assert that changing transition hash changes canonical signature message bytes;
2. call verifier;
3. require `false`.

No crypto code was changed.

This is a useful reminder: distinguish malformed-verification errors from normal cryptographic mismatch results.

```text
explicit Service Node identity
        ↓
explicit logical key ref
        ↓
explicit seed
        ↓
derive deterministic public key
        ↓
construct one concrete process-local KeyId
        ↓
construct ServiceNodeQuorumParticipant
        ↓
construct seed-backed Signer
        ↓
register participant into RuntimeStatus
```

There is no random fallback key.

There is no implicit memory-keystore key generation.

Seed is not logged.

Seed is not returned over HTTP.

The code does **not** claim persistent KMS semantics.

A private-beta public identity log may include:

```text
chain_id
service_node_id
logical_key_ref
public_key
```

but not secret seed.

# 31. Recommended exact implementation sequence next session

## Step 1 — unsigned deterministic committee checkpoint candidate

Implement in `ron-ledger`.

Candidate should require reviewed/canonical root inputs and construct:

```text
QuickChainCommitteeCheckpointPayloadV1
```

Then:

```text
payload.validate()
canonical JSON
BLAKE3(
  quickchain.checkpoint.v1
  || 0x00
  || canonical bytes
)
```

Return a candidate artifact containing at minimum:

```text
payload
checkpoint_hash
```

Potentially retain provenance wrappers for typed roots rather than accepting arbitrary `ContentId`s wherever meaningful.

No signatures.

No finality.

### Tests should include

* same inputs → same bytes/hash;
* reordered caller-side root-material inputs do not change already-canonical roots;
* receipt root must come from typed ledger-sequence provenance;
* change state root → candidate hash changes;
* change receipt root → hash changes;
* change accounting root → hash changes;
* change reward root → hash changes;
* change DA root → hash changes;
* change validator set → hash changes;
* change policy/chain params → hash changes;
* invalid payload rejects before candidate returned;
* no signatures in candidate;
* no finality fields/claims.

Run focused ron-ledger tests and source-boundary scanners.

---

## Step 2 — independent candidate reproduction

Once candidate builder is GREEN, prove multiple independent contexts derive the same checkpoint hash.

The ideal progression:

```text
same reviewed operation batch
        ↓
same deterministic state/receipt/etc roots
        ↓
same committee checkpoint payload
        ↓
same checkpoint hash on multiple nodes
```

This should be deterministic, not coordinated by sharing the already-computed hash.

---

## Step 3 — validator signature contract

Only after candidate reproduction is green:

Create/reuse canonical validator-signature message bytes for:

```text
chain
height
epoch
checkpoint hash
validator identity
key identity
algorithm
```

Avoid caller-supplied alternate checkpoint preimages.

Each validator independently signs the candidate hash.

No validator may finalize alone.

---

## Step 4 — committee validation

Prove:

```text
validator exists in reviewed validator set
validator key matches
signature verifies
duplicate validator signatures reject
unknown validator rejects
wrong chain rejects
wrong height rejects
wrong epoch rejects
wrong checkpoint hash rejects
threshold calculation deterministic
1-of-N insufficient
threshold-of-N accepted
```

This is distinct from the Service Node epoch-transition quorum already proven.

Do not conflate Service Node reward quorum with checkpoint validator committee unless the canonical architecture explicitly says they are the same set.

---

## Step 5 — checkpoint finality artifact

Only then introduce the actual finality/finalized-checkpoint artifact.

It must bind:

```text
unsigned candidate
candidate hash
validator set
threshold
verified unique signatures
finalization state
```

It should not allow:

```text
one process
one signer
one HTTP response
CrabLink
```

to declare finality.

---

## Step 6 — live multi-process checkpoint/finality

Extend the real multi-node process proof.

Goal:

```text
multiple Service Nodes reproduce checkpoint candidate
multiple eligible validators sign it
one signature insufficient
required threshold accepted
member failure still permits threshold if mathematically possible
restart preserves identity
wrong candidate rejected
```

---

## Step 7 — live replay and duplicate rejection

Bring existing deterministic replay protections into the live process context.

Prove at least:

```text
duplicate operation rejected/idempotent
replayed transition rejected
replayed checkpoint signing request does not create contradictory state
duplicate validator signature does not increase quorum count
duplicate Service Node signature does not increase quorum count
```

---

## Step 8 — challenge path

Use the User Node/micronode verifier to challenge:

```text
wrong root
wrong signature
wrong validator set
tampered checkpoint
tampered receipt
tampered transition
```

No fake challenge success strings.

---

## Step 9 — DA/archive fallback

Existing DA fallback model/tests exist.

Bring them into the integrated Phase 19 proof.

Checkpoint commits:

```text
data_availability_root
```

so recovery/fallback must be consistent with that commitment.

---

## Step 10 — reward evidence stays ledger-confirmed

Continue proving that quorum evidence does not itself create ROC.

Required separation:

```text
evidence
→ reviewed reward plan
→ quorum
→ ledger execution
→ durable confirmed receipt
```

Never:

```text
signature count
→ direct mint
```

Single-node mint rejection must remain preserved.

Run actual Phase 19 integrated chaos after deterministic functionality is stable.

Candidate scenarios:

```text
kill one Service Node
restart one Service Node
temporarily lose User Node
replay requests
duplicate requests
malformed checkpoint
stale validator set
wrong signing key
partial network availability
DA fallback
bad signature
wrong checkpoint candidate
```

Do not run huge chaos matrices before basic checkpoint/finality is green.

## Step 12 — soak

Then run a meaningful multi-node soak.

Observe:

```text
process health
deterministic roots
candidate convergence
signature uniqueness
no drift
no memory runaway
no stuck restart
no phantom finality
no duplicate reward execution
```

Only after network truth exists.

CrabLink may display:

```text

degraded state
```

CrabLink may **not** decide finality.

# 35. Important patching lesson from this session

We hit **two patch-script failures caused by formatting-sensitive structural assertions**, not product-code defects.

Examples:

```text
transition_identity.validate()
```

versus multiline rustfmt output.

And:

```text
runtime.quorum_participation_active()
```

versus multiline rustfmt output.

Going forward:

> Patch scripts should avoid requiring Rust expressions to exist on one exact physical line unless line shape itself is the contract.

Prefer checking independent semantic tokens such as:

```text
transition_identity
.validate

quorum_participation_active
```

or parse/inspect broader function regions.

This will preserve momentum and avoid unnecessary rollback/reapply cycles.

# 1. New active CrabNode doctrine

```text
CrabNode
= the complete public RustyOnions Service Node product

crabnode
= the public executable / operator interface

= internal Service Node host/composition implementation

micronode
```

```text
done
```

# 20. Windows Tauri defects fixed this session

There were three meaningful portability issues.

## 20.1 Tauri icon source portability

Initial public source did not make Windows `icon.ico` reliably available because `.gitignore` pattern:

```text
Icon?
```

matched `icons` on case-insensitive Windows.

Fix was committed earlier:

```text
e79144b Track Tauri platform icons for Windows builds
```

Complete Tauri icon resources are now tracked.

---

## 20.2 Bundle icon declaration

Windows release executable compiled, but WiX failed:

```text
Couldn't find a .ico icon
```

Fix:

```json
"bundle": {
  "active": true,
  "targets": "all",
  "icon": [
    "icons/32x32.png",
    "icons/128x128.png",
    "icons/128x128@2x.png",
    "icons/icon.icns",
    "icons/icon.ico"
  ]
}
```

This resulted in real:

```text
MSI = GREEN
NSIS = GREEN
```

---

## 20.3 Tauri macOS private API config mismatch

Global Cargo feature was:

```toml
tauri = { version = "2", features = ["macos-private-api"] }
```

but the base config did not declare the matching Tauri config state.

Tauri would rewrite Cargo features on Windows.

Final fix:

```json
"app": {
  "macOSPrivateApi": true
}
```

along with removal of stale partial-config injection from the Mac Rust-check helper.

Commit:

```text
2079231 Fix cross-platform Tauri build configuration
```

Public Mac and Windows builds now both work.

# 44. Four-plane architecture

Do not treat the whole RustyOnions system like one giant BitTorrent network.

The better model is:

```text
                  CRABNODE NETWORK

1. IMMUTABLE CONTENT PLANE
   b3 objects
   providers
   DHT
   fetch
   verify
   cache
   replication
   repair

2. MUTABLE PUBLIC STATE PLANE
   usernames
   profiles
   site pointers
   tombstones
   signed descriptors
   deterministic transitions

3. ECONOMIC / EVIDENCE PLANE
   delivery evidence
   repair evidence
   accounting
   reward planning
   quorum
   wallet
   ledger
   ROC

4. OPERATOR CONTROL PLANE
   crabnode CLI
   policy
   prune
   persistence
   admin
   status
   logs
```

These planes interact.

They are not the same authority.

---

# 45. Torrent-like content behavior

The useful BitTorrent analogy applies to immutable content.

Correct:

```text
Who has b3:X?
Fetch it.
Verify it.
Cache/persist if policy permits.
Advertise myself as a provider.
Repair missing replication when necessary.
```

Unlike ordinary torrenting, CrabNode adds:

```text
policy
moderation
tombstones
operator blocks
amnesia-first storage
signed provider identity
service evidence
economic rewards
quorum
```

It is best described as:

```text
policy-aware content-addressed swarm distribution
```

---

# 46. DHT is not username consensus

Never implement:

```text
first DHT record seen for @alice wins
```

DHT timing is not a safe uniqueness authority.

Mutable identity requires signed deterministic transitions and eventual network convergence.


Do not use:

```text
ron-ledger
```

as a generic database simply because it already has deterministic/quorum mechanisms.

Economic truth stays economic.

Namespace truth stays its own state domain.

---

# 48. CN-14 — swarm moderation and prune semantics

Rules:

```text
local operator block:
  local refusal only

global signed deny:
  accepted policy propagated to compliant nodes

owner tombstone:
  affects compliant resolution/serving;
  cannot magically erase all existing immutable bytes everywhere

quarantine:
  not served while unresolved

local prune:
  removes local bytes
  removes own provider state
  does not delete remote copies
```

Repair must consult policy before refetching.

A prune command must not lead to immediate automatic reacquisition of the same blocked content.

```text
User Node verification
```

Real evidence should derive from real operations:

```text
verified remote delivery
availability proof/challenge

valid policy refusal
independent verification
```

Reject:

```text
self-fetch farming
replay
duplicate idempotency key
invalid hash
unverified byte counts
service evidence choosing its own payout address
```

Correct payout path:

```text
service_node_id
→ evidence
→ accounting/reward planning
→ policy
→ quorum
→ signed reward recipient binding
→ svc-wallet
→ ron-ledger
→ confirmed receipt/balance
```

One CrabNode cannot pay itself.

The internal ROC doctrine independently preserves wallet/ledger as economic truth and classifies service observations as evidence before payout.

# 59. Security and privacy invariants

Always preserve:

```text
Admin loopback-only by default.
No public admin exposure by accident.
No User Node residential IP publication.
No direct user-user TCP by default.
Capabilities only / no ambient authority.
Unvetted content amnesia-first.
B3 verified before trusted/useful service acceptance.
Unknown fields fail closed where strict DTO/config applies.
Queues/buffers/provider tables bounded.
No locks held across await on hot paths.
No unbounded restart storms.
No raw secrets in logs.
No secrets passed as CLI args where avoidable.
```

---

# 60. Moderation/persistence invariants

Operators must control their own hosted content.

Storage states include concepts such as:

```text
ephemeral_unvetted
pending_review
verified_persistent
operator_blocked
global_denied
owner_tombstoned
quarantined
pinned_by_operator
```

Important:

```text
verified_persistent
```

does **not** automatically mean bytes are already durable.

Do not fake persistence.

A local operator's block/prune decision must not falsely claim global deletion.

# 15. WHY PHYSICAL M1 EXPANDED INTO PASSPORT CRYPTO WORK

The current stored desktop Passport originally had real secure vault material but did **not** yet have a canonical public Passport identity wired into the live product path.

Existing vault already contained:

```text
RecoveryRoot factor
Operational factor
wrapped root VMK
wrapped operational VMK
platform-sealed factors
```

But the operational session only held:

```text
platform family
operational VMK
```

No canonical Passport ID/root public key/device authorization was being surfaced.

Existing status intentionally reported identifier absent/redacted.

So Physical M1 needed to derive the real Passport identity from the existing durable RecoveryRoot rather than creating a new Passport.

---

# 16. CANONICAL NATIVE PASSPORT IDENTITY MODEL

Locked derivation model:

```text
stored RecoveryRoot factor
→ canonical BIP39 entropy/mnemonic
→ BIP39 seed
→ versioned HKDF-SHA256
→ Ed25519 root signing key
→ Ed25519 root public key
→ domain-separated BLAKE3 Passport ID
```

Canonical Passport ID:


# 49. PRE-CREATE NATIVE STATUS REVIEW

`PassportCreateStep` now first calls:

```javascript
readNativePassportStatus()
```

and reviews it.

Rules:

### `no_passport`

```text
safeToCreate=true
```

Only then may native creation be attempted.

### `locked` / `stored_locked`

```text
existing=true
create=false
resume=true
```

### `operational_unlocked`

```text
existing=true
create=false
resume=true
```

### malformed/unsafe/unknown

```text
safeToCreate=false
existing=false
fail closed
```

This means WebView localStorage no longer decides whether native custody exists.

```text
status:
no_passport

another process/state transition creates vault

create:
already_exists
```

New behavior:

```text
already_exists
→ re-read native status

if native status now proves a real vault:
reconcile

otherwise:
retain failure
```

No duplicate create attempt.

# 84. SHELL / ZSH RULES

Interactive zsh environment has:

```text
interactivecomments off
```

Therefore top-level pasted lines beginning with:

```bash
#
```

can cause:

```text
zsh: command not found: #
```

Avoid top-level shell comment lines in paste-ready commands.

Also:

```text
never use zsh variable name:
status
```

It is reserved/read-only.

Avoid unquoted `!`.

Commands should remain paste-ready and readable.

# 3. `ron-proto` Physical M1 authorization work

The canonical protocol-owned Native Passport authorization model is now established.

## Canonical `DeviceClassV1`

The active protocol vocabulary is exactly:

```text
root_admin_desktop
root_admin_mobile
personal_desktop
personal_mobile
tv_read_only
recovery_only
test_harness
```

The older `svc-passport::native::dto::DeviceClass` values:

```text
tv_read_only
desktop_read_only
mobile_read_only
```

are historical Phase-3 contract types and must **not** be promoted into the current `DeviceAuthorizationV1` policy.

The current canonical seven-class vocabulary is owned by `ron-proto`. 

## Canonical `DeviceAuthorizationV1`

The protocol shape now includes:

```text
version
network_id
environment
passport_id
root_key_epoch
device_id
device_public_key
device_class
authorized_scope_ceiling
authorization_nonce
issued_at_ms
expires_at_ms?
root_signature
```

Critical trust rule:

```text
root_public_key IS NOT supplied by the authorization wire.
```

The trusted root public key comes from trusted verification context / canonical Passport root state.

Other locked rules:

```text
version = 1
nonce = exactly 16 bytes
signature = exactly 64 bytes
network/environment labels bounded
scope tokens bounded
max scopes = 32
scope ceiling sorted + unique
unknown fields rejected where strict DTO applies
optional expiry must be later than issuance
binary fields use base64url without padding
```

The wire implementation and tests are visible in the RustyOnions bundle. 

## Frozen ID authority

Canonical ID domains are owned by `ron-proto`, while the already-released physical derivation remains unchanged.

Passport ID hash input remains:

```text
domain|main|ed25519|root_public_key_hex
```

Device ID remains:

```text
domain|ed25519|device_public_key_hex
```

Do not alter these derivations to match any newer theoretical structured encoding.

# 4. `ron-auth` Physical M1 authorization work

`ron-auth` now owns the canonical signing transcript and strict verification.

## Canonical transcript

Domain:

```text
rustyonions.native-passport.device-authorization.v1
```

Canonical encoding:

```text
length-prefixed-binary-v1
```

Historical Phase-0 encoding remains:

```text
pipe-delimited-canonical-v1
```

but is explicitly **not signable**.

JSON is also explicitly non-signable.

The canonical transcript is a deterministic binary structure using:

```text
LP(domain)
u16 version
LP(network)
LP(environment)
LP(passport_id)
u64 root_key_epoch
LP(device_id)
LP(raw device public key)
LP(device class)
u16 scope count
repeated LP(scope)
LP(raw 16-byte nonce)
u64 issued_at
u8 expiry-present
optional u64 expiry
```

where `LP` is a big-endian length-prefixed field.

The frozen test baseline remains:

```text
PHYSICAL_M1_BINARY_TRANSCRIPT_BYTES=480
PHYSICAL_M1_BINARY_TRANSCRIPT_B3=
d8dc1fc08383f61dbc5115daafff9fed7fcacfa52f7a1c9c42b5250cf1a191a7
```

The terminal reconfirmed the locked transcript tests at **3/3 green** this session. The implementation is also present in the RustyOnions bundle. 

## Strict verifier

The strict verifier checks:

```text
authorization validation
trusted root public key validity
trusted root → Passport-ID binding
authorization Passport-ID binding
device public key → Device-ID binding
network match
environment match
root epoch match
issued-at/skew
expiry/skew
canonical transcript reconstruction
strict Ed25519 signature verification
```

It rejects:

```text
wrong root
wrong Passport
wrong device binding
field mutations
signature mutation
wrong signer
BLAKE3-digest signatures
JSON signatures
legacy pipe-transcript signatures
```

Latest reconfirmation:

```text
RON_AUTH_STRICT_VERIFIER_FINAL_REGRESSION=GREEN
7 passed
```

The strict verifier tests and trusted-context model are captured in the RustyOnions bundle.

# 6. Root-signing architecture implemented in `svc-passport`

## New file

```text
crates/svc-passport/src/native/device_authorization_signing.rs
```

This is the public, purpose-specific DeviceAuthorization signer.

It does **not** expose:

```text
SigningKey
raw-message signing
generic root signing
HKDF output
root seed
filesystem access
Keychain access
network access
capability issuance
username mutation
wallet/ledger authority
```

The current code is visible in the fresh `svc-passport` bundle. 

## Signing sequence

`sign_native_device_authorization_v1(...)` now:

```text
1. validates DeviceAuthorizationSigningPayloadV1
2. derives canonical root public identity from supplied BIP-39 seed
3. verifies payload.passport_id matches the derived Passport
4. bridges the device public key into the native canonical type
5. rederives the Device ID from that public key
6. verifies payload.device_id matches
7. invokes the narrow root-specific signing primitive
8. builds DeviceAuthorizationV1
```

Errors include:

```text
InvalidPayload
RootIdentityDerivationFailed
PassportBindingMismatch
DevicePublicKeyBridgeFailed
DeviceIdDerivationFailed
DeviceIdBindingMismatch
RootSignatureFailed
SignedAuthorizationConstructionFailed
```

No persistence occurs here.

Therefore:

```text
signature creation != server authorization registration
```

That distinction must remain.

# 7. `root_identity.rs` custody refactor

The root derivation implementation was refactored so the frozen HKDF path has one internal owner.

Important private helper:

```text
with_native_root_signing_key_v1(...)
```

This owns the existing frozen:

```text
BIP39 seed
    ↓
HKDF-SHA256
    ↓
32-byte Ed25519 root seed
    ↓
SigningKey
```

A narrow sibling-visible helper was added for **only**:

```text
DeviceAuthorizationSigningPayloadV1
```

It obtains canonical transcript bytes from `ron-auth` and signs those exact bytes.

There is no:

```text
pub SigningKey
pub root signing seed
generic sign(bytes)
arbitrary-message root signer
```

This is an important security boundary to preserve.

# 12. CrabLink root-signing inventory conclusions

The newer CrabLink bundle was very useful here. 

## Existing `passport_unlock_root` must NOT become the signing command

Current root confirmation behavior is designed around identity finalization.

Once the public descriptor exists, the command intentionally returns:

```text
IdentityAvailable
```

without:

```text
prompting root PIN again
unsealing RecoveryRoot again
```

That is correct for identity reads.

It is **not** correct for a new root signature.

Root-signing rule going forward:

```text
every new root-authority signature requires a fresh explicit native confirmation
```

Do not create a reusable "root unlocked" session.

## Existing native secret surface is reusable

CrabLink already has:

```text
DesktopNativeSecretSurfacePort
request_root_confirmation_pin()
```

This keeps PIN entry outside React/WebView.

Reuse it.

Never add:

```text
#[tauri::command]
fn ...(pin: String)
```

or equivalent.

## Existing root PIN verification path is usable

Current identity finalization already knows how to:

```text
load versioned vault
base_v1()
unseal RecoveryRoot platform factor
verify RecoveryRoot PIN
derive root public identity
```

This is the correct platform custody foundation.

## Existing V2 device public-identity reader is canonical

Use:

```text
read_desktop_native_passport_session_device_public_identity(...)
```

It:

```text
requires operational-unlocked session
borrows operational VMK synchronously
decrypts authenticated V2 operational payload
rederives public device identity
verifies persisted public-key binding
returns only NativeDevicePublicIdentityV1
```

Do not rederive device identity in React.

Do not decrypt the device payload in a new ad-hoc command.

## No current desktop DeviceAuthorization command

The inventory found no existing desktop DeviceAuthorization wiring.

Candidate filenames remained available:

```text
src-tauri/src/passport_device_authorization_command_runtime.rs

src-tauri/tests/
physical_m1_desktop_device_authorization_command.rs
```

So we can add the new boundary cleanly later without colliding with an older implementation.

mapping.

# 20. Dedicated CrabLink signing command design

Once policy/context is green, implement a **new dedicated command**, not an extension of `passport_unlock_root`.

Conceptual sequence:

```text
Tauri command invoked
    ↓
require stored Passport
    ↓
require operational session unlocked
    ↓
load durable public Passport descriptor
    ↓
read canonical physical V2 device public identity
    ↓
construct policy-owned signing context
    ↓
native request_root_confirmation_pin()
    ↓
unseal RecoveryRoot factor
    ↓
verify PIN against RecoveryRoot wrapped VMK
    ↓
call svc-passport recovery-factor signer
    ↓
drop recovery factor/root-related transient material
    ↓
strictly verify returned public authorization through ron-auth
    ↓
return only public DeviceAuthorizationV1
```

Never return:

```text
PIN
RecoveryRoot factor
mnemonic
BIP-39 seed
root Ed25519 seed
SigningKey
root VMK
operational VMK
device signing seed
```

# 21. No persistent root-unlocked session

This must remain an explicit invariant.

Correct model:

```text
ordinary application operation
    -> device key

root-authority mutation
    -> fresh native root confirmation
    -> one narrow operation
    -> root material disappears
```

Incorrect model:

```text
user entered root PIN once
    -> root remains globally unlocked indefinitely
```

Do not build the second model.

---

# 22. Signed DeviceAuthorization persistence still needs design

Once a test/native command can safely create an authorization, decide how to persist it.

Do **not** mutate the frozen V2 operational payload ad hoc.

V2 currently has a narrow purpose:

```text
base V1 vault
+
encrypted operational device seed/public binding
```

A root-signed authorization is public authority metadata and likely belongs in a separate versioned public record/store.

Requirements should include:

```text
strict schema
version
atomic write
restart recovery
binding to Passport
binding to device
root epoch
nonce
issue/expiry
signature
no secret material
corruption fails closed
```

Then strict verification must occur before accepting persisted authorization after restart.

Only after the local signed authorization is real:

```text
svc-passport durable DeviceAuthorization registry
challenge issuance

/v1/passport/challenge
/v1/passport/prove
device possession proof
authorization lookup
root epoch validation
expiry validation
nonce/replay rejection
device-bound capability issuance
```

Server truth remains in `svc-passport`.

# 29. Key security distinctions to retain

### DeviceKey

The macOS Keychain `device-key` value is a **platform factor**.

It is **not** the Ed25519 device signing seed.

Never repurpose it.

### Device signing seed

Lives inside:

```text
V2 encrypted operational-device payload
```

under the operational VMK.

### Root authority

Derived from:

```text
RecoveryRoot
→ canonical mnemonic
→ BIP39 seed
→ frozen HKDF
→ Ed25519 root key
```

### Root public key

Trusted root public key is external verification context.

It is never trusted from `DeviceAuthorizationV1` itself.

5. Canonical signed challenge protocol added to ron-proto

Live inspection proved there was previously no real Native Passport PassportChallengeV1. The old svc-passport Phase 8A challenge implementation was intentionally contract-only and explicitly said that service challenge signing/verification/runtime were absent.

We therefore created the real protocol-owned challenge model.

Protocol ownership
PASSPORT_CHALLENGE_V1_PROTOCOL_OWNER=RON_PROTO
PASSPORT_CHALLENGE_PURPOSE_OWNER=RON_PROTO

The old svc-passport challenge layer now aliases the protocol-owned purpose enum rather than owning a duplicate enum.

That is important: do not create another challenge purpose state machine or enum in svc-passport.

PassportChallengePurposeV1

The current closed V1 purpose vocabulary contains:

RegisterRoot
AuthorizeDevice
RevokeDevice
ProveSession
IssueCapability
RefreshCapability
ClaimUsername
TransferUsername
ReleaseUsername
PublishProfile
RegisterSite
UpdateSite
WalletAuthorizationRequestReserved

The wallet authorization variant is reserved and rejected by current V1 validation.

No live wallet authority was enabled.

Canonical signed challenge fields

PassportChallengeSigningPayloadV1 / PassportChallengeV1 bind the following public data:

version
challenge_id

network_id
environment
audience

issuing_service_id
service_key_id

purpose
requested_scopes

passport_id          optional depending on purpose
device_id            optional depending on purpose
operation_body_hash  optional depending on purpose

nonce

issued_at_ms
expires_at_ms

service_signature    on PassportChallengeV1
Challenge validation rules now include
only V1;
reserved wallet purpose rejected;
requested scopes must not be empty;
max scope count remains bounded by existing Native Passport limits;
scopes must be canonical/sorted;
duplicates rejected;
purpose-specific Passport binding enforced;
purpose-specific Device binding enforced;
purpose-specific operation body hash enforced;
issued_at_ms nonzero;
expiry strictly after issue;
challenge TTL bounded to 300 seconds;
unknown JSON fields rejected.
Clock-skew design

A useful architectural correction was made during this session:

CLOCK_SKEW_WIRE_FIELD=NO
CLOCK_SKEW_IS_TRUSTED_VERIFIER_POLICY=YES

The challenge does not tell the verifier how much skew to tolerate.

The current V1 ceiling is:

PASSPORT_CHALLENGE_V1_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS=30000

The verifier chooses trusted skew policy locally, subject to that protocol ceiling.

Do not put caller-provided or request-provided clock-skew tolerance into authority-bearing challenge input.

Challenge TTL
PASSPORT_CHALLENGE_V1_MAX_TTL_MS=300000

Maximum challenge lifetime is five minutes.

10. KMS signing identity / rotation boundary repaired

The second integration issue found during inspection was more important cryptographically.

The existing KmsClient API had:

sign(message) -> (kid, signature)

but did not let a Native Passport challenge issuer choose/bind a specific KID before constructing the signed transcript.

That is unsafe around rotation because the KID is part of the challenge transcript.

We specifically avoided this bad design:

sign once
discover returned KID
rewrite challenge
sign again

and avoided inventing an unstable KID normalization.

New KMS public signing identity

svc-passport/src/kms/client.rs now exposes a public-only signing identity DTO equivalent to:

KmsSigningIdentity {
    kid
    public_key
}

No private signing key leaves the KMS.

New KMS methods

The trait gained authority-sensitive seams equivalent to:

active_signing_identity()
sign_with_kid(kid, message)

Crucially, their trait defaults are fail-closed.

That means an injected external/production KMS implementation does not silently gain Native Passport challenge-signing authority merely because the trait was extended.

Marker:

EXTERNAL_KMS_NEW_AUTHORITY_DEFAULT=FAIL_CLOSED

Existing KMS APIs were preserved:

sign
verify
public_keys
rotate
attest

This avoided breaking legacy issuer/JWKS behavior.

DevKms rotation hardening

The development KMS previously stored the current version and key material through separate synchronization pieces.

It now keeps current signing state under one lock:

version
kid
signing_key
verifying_key
history

This prevents a reader from observing a KID/public-key pair inconsistent with the signing key during rotation.

Rotation generates new random key material before taking the write lock and performs the current-state swap atomically under the lock.

No .await occurs while the lock is held.

sign_with_kid fails if the requested KID is no longer the active KID.

Thus:

preselect KID v1
rotate to KID v2
attempt sign_with_kid(v1)
=> REJECT

Historical public-key verification remains available, so signatures made before rotation still verify using the historical KID.

New focused KMS test

Created:

crates/svc-passport/tests/
physical_m1_service_challenge_kms_identity.rs

It proves:

selected KID/public key agree
exact-KID signature verifies
legacy sign still works
rotation changes KID/public key
old preselected KID cannot sign after rotation
new KID signs successfully
historical pre-rotation signature still verifies

KMS_IDENTITY_TESTS=2_GREEN

17. Immediate next implementation: durable one-time challenge/replay state

This is the exact next task:

NEXT_ACTION=DURABLE_ONE_TIME_CHALLENGE_REPLAY_STATE

The real private issuer should now be wrapped by durable server state.

Required high-level state machine

At minimum the runtime needs truthful server-owned states equivalent to:

issued
consumed
expired
cancelled

Challenge state must survive process restart.

A challenge that has been consumed must never become usable again after restart.

A cancelled challenge must not become usable again.

An expired challenge must not become usable merely because the server restarted.

Issuance durability rule

Do not return a usable challenge to a caller before the issued state is durably committed.

Safe conceptual sequence:

build/sign/strict-verify challenge
attempt durable issued-state commit
fsync / durable success
only then return challenge

If persistence fails, the signature may have been produced internally, but the signed challenge must not be exposed as successful issuance.

Do not fake success because signing succeeded.

Store full authoritative binding

The durable record must be sufficient to prove exactly which signed challenge was issued.

At minimum it must be impossible to substitute a different:

challenge_id
nonce
network
environment
audience
issuing_service
service_key_id
purpose
requested scopes
passport binding
device binding
operation body hash
issue time
expiry
challenge transcript/signature binding

Whether the best representation is the complete PassportChallengeV1, a canonical immutable record plus signature, or an exact transcript hash should be decided from live source and restart requirements.

Do not create an ambiguous reduced representation.

Replay behavior

Required negative cases should include:

unknown challenge
already consumed challenge
cancelled challenge
expired challenge
wrong challenge payload/hash
wrong purpose
wrong subject binding
wrong operation body
wrong scopes
wrong service key/signature
stale generation / concurrent mutation

All should fail closed.

Concurrent consumption

Two concurrent attempts at the same challenge must never both win.

Required outcome:

exactly one successful consumption
all other concurrent attempts rejected as replay/already-consumed

Use real compare-and-swap/generation semantics or another explicit single-winner mechanism.

Do not rely only on in-memory locks because restart durability is part of the requirement.

Bounded state

Challenge/replay state must remain bounded.

Do not create an unbounded forever-growing list.

Implement explicit pruning/retention for terminal expired/consumed/cancelled records while preserving enough tombstone/replay history to make the replay guarantee truthful.

The exact retention design should be inspected against the Native Passport buildplan before committing.

Persistence hardening

Reuse the quality bar already established by server_registry_store:

strict schema/version
unknown fields rejected
atomic generation transition
fsync durability
private permissions
symlink/non-file rejection
corruption fail-closed
restart recovery
lost-update rejection
bounded state
deterministic ordering

Prefer reuse of the existing durable snapshot patterns rather than inventing an unrelated persistence style.

18. Most important next architectural problem: challenge consumption + root registration atomicity

This deserves special attention.

We currently have two separate durable concepts:

A. challenge/replay state
B. root registry state

The root registration runtime is already generation-CAS durable.

The challenge runtime will also need durable one-time consumption.

We must not implement:

consume challenge
then write root

or:

write root
then consume challenge

and casually label it atomic.

A crash between two independent durable commits can leave inconsistent state.

For example:

root write succeeds
process crashes before challenge consumption

could leave the root registered but the challenge apparently still usable.

The root-registration runtime is intentionally idempotent, which is helpful, but idempotency alone is not proof of atomic one-time challenge consumption.

Next session should explicitly design crash recovery before mounting routes.

Potential approaches include a recoverable transaction/journal or another composition that can prove deterministic recovery, but inspect the current stores/contracts before choosing. Do not introduce a second competing durable registry or silently weaken the one-time requirement.

Required tests should eventually inject/reproduce failure at every durable transition boundary.

19. Root registration flow once replay state exists

The intended real server registration sequence should become approximately:

client asks svc-passport for RegisterRoot challenge

svc-passport:
  derives trusted network/environment/audience/time
  builds purpose-bound request
  private issuer signs challenge
  durably records challenge as issued
  returns signed PassportChallengeV1

client:
  verifies svc-passport service signature
  verifies intended purpose/context/body
  recovery/root key signs canonical ron-auth root-registration proof

svc-passport:
  locates exact issued challenge
  verifies service challenge binding/state
  verifies root proof cryptographically
  re-derives Passport ID from concrete root public key
  applies trusted initial root epoch rules
  atomically establishes durable root + one-time challenge consumption
  returns truthful result

No arbitrary subject registration.

Backend never generates the user's Passport root key.

Recovery/root secret material remains local.

strict ron-auth DeviceAuthorization verification
svc-passport recovery/root DeviceAuthorization signer
existing native device key/ID flow
ron-policy device scope ceilings
durable server device registry records

Do not create another device authorization format.

Server must validate at current trusted server time/context:

Passport/root binding
root epoch
network
environment
device public key / Device ID
device class
authorized scope ceiling
authorization nonce
issue/expiry
root signature
ron-policy scope ceiling

Then require proof of possession of the device private key before treating the device as active network authority.

No personal device escalation beyond ron-policy.

# 8. Existing durable RegisterRoot coordinator

This is one of the most important completed pieces.

The server coordinator owns the actual crash-recoverable authority transaction:

```text
validate challenge + proof binding

        ↓

persist immutable redo intent

        ↓

consume exact one-time challenge

        ↓

idempotently register Passport root

        ↓

clear redo intent
```

Do not duplicate this state machine in HTTP handlers, Omnigate, gateway, CrabLink or macronode.

Already-green coordinator behavior includes:

```text
proof-binding mismatch never writes redo intent

normal transaction:
challenge consumed
root registered
intent cleared

restart after durable intent:
recovers

restart after challenge consumption:
recovers

restart after root registration before intent completion:
recovers

accepted_at remains immutable during recovery
```

The newest `svc-passport` implementation continues to call the existing coordinator rather than creating another transaction path.

# 11. Important Omnigate policy issue found and repaired this session

The first real public challenge attempt reached Omnigate but returned:

```json
{
  "code": "POLICY_DENY",
  "reason": "default"
}
```

HTTP:

```text
403
```

This was correctly diagnosed as a policy-classification problem rather than a routing failure.

The loaded policy bundle:

```text
default_action = deny
```

and previously admitted only safe read methods.

We did **not**:

```text
disable policy
allow all POSTs
add a development bypass
trust a caller-selected header
change ron-policy's schema to invent path matching
```

Instead, Omnigate now derives a trusted local classification tag from the exact method+URI for the reviewed challenge route.

Tag:

```text
cn4-fixed-identity-admission
```

The policy allows POST only when that trusted tag is present.

Properties proven:

```text
DEFAULT_DENY=PRESERVED
EXACT_REGISTERROOT_CHALLENGE_POST=ALLOWED
DIFFERENT_POST=DENIED
CALLER_HEADER_TAG_INJECTION=REJECTED
GLOBAL_POST_ALLOW=NO
POLICY_DISABLED=NO
```

This is an important security result.

```text
denied before routing
```

# 17. Server reconstructs the canonical proof transcript

`submit_register_root_proof_durable` reconstructs the canonical server-side transcript from:

```text
the signed challenge

plus

the concrete root public key

plus

proof creation time

plus

trusted runtime configuration
```

Server-derived fields include:

```text
challenge transcript B3 hash

challenge contract domain/version

proof contract domain/version

network

environment

audience

passport binding

operation body hash

requested scopes

challenge issue/expiry times

trusted initial root epoch
```

The implementation uses the canonical `ron-auth` challenge transcript hash and the existing `RootRegistrationProofTranscriptV1`, then feeds it into the existing crash-recoverable coordinator.

This preserves the correct ownership model:

```text
HTTP layer:
parses bounded evidence

runtime layer:
reconstructs trusted transcript

coordinator:
owns mutation transaction

registry:
owns durable root authority
```

```text
Phase 23
UX / Accessibility / Performance

Phase 24
Desktop Packaging / Signing / Update / Recovery

Phase 25
Private Beta Operations

Phase 26
Final Acceptance / Launch
```

Phase 22 includes secret scans, sandbox corpus, replay, rate limits, moderation and privacy boundaries. 

Phase 23 includes UX, keyboard/screen-reader accessibility, contrast, startup and long-session performance. 

Phase 24 requires actual installable/signable beta artifacts and migration/recovery behavior. 

Phase 25 is the controlled invite-only operational posture. 

Phase 26 reruns automated and manual final acceptance before an honest beta release decision.
